title: What the Eye Receives
logline: At a free cataract camp, dressings come off one by one, and each patient's first sight in months arrives before anyone can film their face changing.

object.note: Object 7 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From an ear straining against the wind to eyes waiting behind dressings: a free eye camp, and first sight arriving after months.

thread_out.thread: Sight restored becomes the body named part by part: young novices reciting its thirty-two parts, an echo of the novices in 'Learning the Map' who memorised the mind.

requirements: A free cataract or eye camp with institutional permission to film
Patients and families giving full informed consent
A camp large enough to allow following a small number of individual stories

suggestions.name: A rural hospital or temple hall hosting a free eye camp
suggestions.why: Free eye camps are a regularly run form of rural healthcare outreach in these provinces.
suggestions.verify: A specific camp, its organisers and willing patients are unverified.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Seeing depends on a small, delicate part of the living body working at all. Because we hold our senses as the most truly 'mine' of anything in us, losing one and getting it back is felt so deeply.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: දැකීම රඳා පවතින්නේ ශරීරයේ ඉතා සියුම් කොටසක් නිසි ලෙස ක්‍රියා කිරීම මත බවත්, අප ඉන්ද්‍රියයන් වඩාත්ම 'මගේ' ලෙස අල්ලා ගන්නා නිසා එකක් නැති වී නැවත ලැබීම එතරම් ගැඹුරින් දැනෙන බවත් මෙයින් පෙනේ.
lesson.the_teaching: Among the twenty-eight kinds of matter are five sensitive kinds, in the eye, ear, nose, tongue and body. The texts distinguish the eye as a whole organ from the sensitive matter within it, and describe that sensitivity as a clear quality of the four great elements themselves rather than a separate thing. When matter is classified, only these five sensitive kinds are called 'internal', not because of where they sit but because the grip of 'me' and 'mine' is strongest there; and of all twenty-eight kinds, only colour can be seen.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film waits with the patients through the dawn queue, the examinations and the long quiet, then stays in the room as dressings come off one at a time. What people say they missed seeing most, and how their families react, lets the viewer feel how much of a person's world rests on one small working part of the body, without the narration naming it.

key_terms.en: sensitive matter in eye, ear, nose, tongue and body
internal (the five sense organs only) / external

lesson.caution: The texts' descriptions of where and how the sense sits in the eye are traditional teaching, not ophthalmology, and nothing here says anything about why any person's sight fails or whether it is deserved.
lesson.builds_on: The landing site showed the ear straining to pick a voice out of the wind; this film follows the eye, where a sense can be clouded and then restored, and shows why the senses feel like the most personal part of the body.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
